*Reasoning in my own voice (Old Wang, 64, middle school):*

Alright, let me think through this year. I'm getting older now and it's just me and the wife at home — both kids work in town. So labor is tight. Can't be too ambitious.

I've got 10.1 mu. Same as the last few years, I'll do about 7 mu wheat-maize double crop and keep about 3 mu in cotton. The cotton is hard work — picking takes weeks and my back isn't what it used to be — but the price has been okay and we need the cash. I thought about dropping cotton entirely but my neighbor Old Liu still does it and he says the buyers are still coming, so I'll keep my small patch.

**Wheat (about 7 mu):** I'll plant in early October like always, around the 8th to 12th. I use that "Jimai 22" type variety — saved some seed from last year's harvest, plus I'll buy a bag of fresh seed to mix in. The extension guy keeps telling us 15 kg N per mu is enough but I always do a bit more, maybe 18 kg total — half urea before planting, the rest topdressed at jointing in March. Last year the wheat looked a little yellow at jointing so I'm not cutting back. I'll need to irrigate 3 times probably — once before winter, once at jointing, once at grain fill. The well still works fine but the electricity bill adds up.

**Maize (same 7 mu, after wheat):** Right after wheat harvest in mid-June I plant maize, no time to waste — usually within 3-4 days. Have to buy hybrid seed every year, can't save it. I use the "Zhengdan 958" type, about 4 kg per mu. Same fertilizer pattern, around 15 kg N per mu, mostly compound fertilizer at planting and a urea topdress at the big-flare stage. Usually only need to irrigate once or twice — summer rains help. If a typhoon comes through I might lose some to lodging but you can't do much about that.

**Cotton (about 3 mu):** Plant late April, around the 25th. I use Bt cotton seed from the agricultural supply shop — costs more but the bollworms aren't as bad as the old days. About 12 kg N per mu, plus some phosphate. The hard part is the spraying — aphids, mirids, sometimes spider mites — I might spray 4 or 5 times through the summer. And then the picking, that's 3-4 rounds from September through October. The wife and I do it ourselves, no money for hired help on this little patch.

For tillage I rent the rotovator from the village service team — costs a bit per mu but I can't run that machine myself anymore.

Money's tight. I'm not buying any fancy inputs. I'll spend what I have to spend and not a yuan more.
